clues.title: Plate: white with a hint of blue on the left
text: When blurred, the standard Kazakh licence plates are mostly white, with a small hint of blue on the left side.

images.caption: Kazakh plates: standard long and short

clues.summary: Through the blur, plates look mostly white with a small bit of blue on the left side.

clues.title: Language: Cyrillic and Latin, Kazakh letters
text: Kazakhstan uses both Cyrillic and Latin alphabets.
Though sometimes, Russian is used monolingually.
- The following letters are found in the Kazakh but not Russian alphabet: Ә (Ä), Ғ (Ǵ), Қ (Q), Ң (Ń), Ө (Ö), Ұ (W), Ү (Ü), Һ (H), І (I).
- Kazakh is related to Turkish, so the Latin text can appear similar.

images.caption: Kazakh text with its special Cyrillic letters, with a Latin version beside it

clues.summary: Signs use Cyrillic and Latin letters, and sometimes only Russian. Kazakh has extra letters such as Ә, Ғ, Қ, Ң, Ө, Ұ, Ү, Һ and І. Its Latin text can look like Turkish.

clues.title: Google car: white pickup, visible or blurred
text: All of the coverage in Kazakhstan was taken with a white pickup truck, which can either be fully visible or mostly blurred.
clues.summary: All coverage uses a white pickup truck, either fully visible or mostly blurred.

clues.title: Landscape: big, empty, flat and open
text: Kazakhstan is a big and diverse country, which features a plethora of distinct landscapes like [deserts](https://goo.gl/maps/DWJvw2JjfZTTF2ER9), [grassy steppes](https://goo.gl/maps/FtuwHnxx1cACr5HU9), [mountain passes](https://goo.gl/maps/dnJR7qdEBDQLUkUC9), and [birch forests](https://goo.gl/maps/NTfW9tkDsF2mVbqT8).
Most strikingly, most of the rural coverage in Kazakhstan is in a very empty, open and mostly flat landscape.
clues.summary: A huge country with deserts, grassy steppe, mountain passes and birch forests. Most rural coverage is very empty, open and mostly flat.

clues.title: Infrastructure: looks like Russia
text: A lot of Kazakh infrastructure, from pedestrian signs, poles, houses, to bollards, is very similar to what you see in Russia.
clues.summary: Pedestrian signs, poles, houses and bollards all look very similar to Russia's, so look for other clues to separate them.

clues.title: Sign: yellow-white crossing stripes
text: Like Russia, Kazakhstan uses **yellow and white stripes** on their pedestrian crossings. However, unlike Russia the stripes often have white dashes on either side. Sometimes, you can find the [dashes](https://goo.gl/maps/sXKtyw86YGYSEKLY9) without the stripes.
clues.summary: Pedestrian crossings use yellow and white stripes as in Russia, but here there are often white dashes on both sides. Sometimes you see just the dashes.

differs.how: Russian stripes have no white dashes beside them

clues.title: Street sign: blue, on buildings, QR code
text: Street Signs in Kazakhstan are often attached to buildings and are **blue **in colour, with white intricate patterns on the top and bottom. They are usually **bilingual or trilingual** and can also contain a **QR code**.
NOTE: They are often inconsistent, with many designs being found in a single city.
clues.summary: Blue street signs fixed to buildings with white patterns at the top and bottom. They are often in two or three languages and may have a QR code. Designs vary even within one city.

clues.title: Bollard: post-Soviet type, 90-degree pair
text: Kazakhstan uses a variety of post-Soviet style bollards, as well as ones that resemble Turkish bollards. Notably, the bollards seemingly consisting of two thin bollards attached at a **90° angle** are unique to Kazakhstan.
clues.summary: Mixed post-Soviet style bollards, some like Turkish ones. The standout is a bollard made of two thin posts joined at a right angle, found only here.

clues.title: Plants: tree trunks painted white at the base
text: The bottom of tree trunks are very often **painted white**.
NOTE: This is common in several eastern European countries, as well as in parts of Russia.
clues.summary: The bottom of tree trunks is very often painted white. This is also common in several eastern European countries and parts of Russia.

clues.title: Chevron: yellow and black
text: Unlike neighbouring countries, Kazakhstan primarily uses **yellow and black** chevrons, except on T Intersections, where you will find the more generic [red and white chevrons](https://goo.gl/maps/PBScqLGeZf5WhaJa7).
clues.summary: Curve chevrons are mostly yellow and black, unlike neighbouring countries. At T-junctions they are the usual red and white.

clues.title: Pipes: gas pipes running above ground in towns
text: Gas pipes are extremely common in Kazakh cities.
clues.summary: Gas pipes running along buildings and streets are extremely common in towns and cities.

clues.title: Ornament: ram's-horn pattern
text: This **ornamental pattern** known as the koshkar-muiz can be found as part of decorations in all kinds of settings in Kazakhstan.
clues.summary: A decorative pattern called koshkar-muiz (ram's horns) appears on all kinds of decorations.

clues.title: Entrance arcs: ornate arches at town entrances
text: Many cities and towns in Kazakhstan have these entrance arcs, which are often quite intricate and ornate.
clues.summary: Many towns have an arch at the entrance, often quite detailed and ornate.

clues.title: Coverage: main roads and cities only
text: Coverage in Kazakhstan is fairly limited. While most major roads and cities are covered, coverage on small rural roads is fairly uncommon. As such, knowing which roads have coverage can help narrow down the guess.
clues.summary: Most major roads and cities are covered, but small rural roads rarely are. Knowing which roads have coverage helps narrow your guess.

clues.title: Coverage: season tells you the region
text: Kazakhstan can easily be divided into coverage regions based on the season.
- **Summer **in **western **and** central **Kazakhstan.
- **Autumn **in the **northeast**.
- **Winter** in the** southeast.**
clues.summary: Coverage season hints at where you are: summer in the west and centre, autumn in the northeast, winter in the southeast.

clues.title: Driving direction on rural roads
text: **Driving directions** can help you narrow down your options when you are on a rural road.
clues.summary: On a rural road, the direction the car is driving can help you narrow down where you are.

clues.title: Phone numbers: area codes run east to west
text: Kazakh area codes are useful to learn, and they generally follow an east to west pattern along three horizontal lines.
clues.summary: Area codes follow an east-to-west pattern along three horizontal bands. Worth learning.

clues.title: Plate: region code on trucks and buses
text: You can occasionally spot licence plate codes on the back of [trucks](https://maps.app.goo.gl/tKZW4WNWfm8LC6Bf8) and [buses](https://goo.gl/maps/ShsB6GNeCf3cp4gB6). The codes themselves follow an alphabetical order, with smaller numbers corresponding to regions that start with earlier letters. Note that cars do travel, and as such not all codes are reliable. Buses and smaller utility vehicles are the most reliable.
clues.summary: The region code is sometimes visible on the back of trucks and buses. Codes follow alphabetical order of the regions. Buses and small utility vehicles are the most reliable, since cars travel.

clues.title: Street sign: letters under the QR code
text: While rarely possible, being able to read the letters under a QR code on a street sign will give you the region.
clues.summary: If you can read the letters under the QR code on a street sign, they tell you the region. This is rarely possible.

clues.title: Landscape: mostly flat, so hills help
text: Kazakhstan is a generally flat country, so getting locations that are hilly or mountainous are useful for narrowing the options.
For example, the region around Karaganda is often either [quite hilly](https://goo.gl/maps/FjDGLgLundGni8JW9), or you can see [hills in the distance](https://goo.gl/maps/SCZGbpzayibTNtp18).
Another [notable set of hills](https://goo.gl/maps/8c3KnWMUZDxPyRv69) would be the ones around Aktobe.
And of course getting bigger mountains will mean you are in the [south](https://goo.gl/maps/5NMT4EMQVSw7s1g27), or [east](https://goo.gl/maps/BdLnnfBacQn6G2XA8).
clues.summary: The country is mostly flat, so hills or mountains help narrow it down. Hills near Karaganda and Aktobe, and bigger mountains in the south or east.

clues.title: Vegetation: lush birch forests by green fields
text: These **lush birch forests** next to green fields are common in northern Kazakhstan.
NOTE: This landscape often appears very similar to that found in and around [Omsk Oblast](https://goo.gl/maps/GSSXj16AyYgmrd2L8) in Russia.
clues.summary: Lush birch forests beside green fields are common in the north. They look very like the area around Omsk in Russia.

clues.title: Landscape: vast green plains
text: **Vast grassy green plains** are found in northwestern Kazakhstan. They are especially common in Akmola and Kostanay regions.
clues.summary: Huge green grass plains in the northwest, especially in Akmola and Kostanay regions.

clues.title: Landscape: sandy shrubby desert in the southwest
text: **Sandy **and shrubby **desert-like** landscapes are common in southwestern Kazakhstan.
clues.summary: Sandy, shrubby desert-like land is common in the southwest.

clues.title: Landscape: tall snow-capped mountains
text: **Tall mountains**, which are often **snow-capped**, can be seen in southeastern Kazakhstan.
clues.summary: Tall mountains, often with snow on top, point to the southeast.

clues.title: Vegetation: hilly forest with autumn colours
text: The East Kazakhstan Region is **hilly **and **forested**. It was covered in october, so you will see **fall colours** on the vegetation. The town of [Ridder](https://goo.gl/maps/i5kesJk8N1Nm9tJK9) itself is flat, but surrounded by hazy mountains.
clues.summary: Hilly, forested land with autumn colours, shot in October, in the far east. One town there is flat but ringed by hazy mountains.

clues.title: Coverage: snow in the southeast
text: **Snow **coverage can be found in **southeastern **Kazakhstan, especially east of Almaty.
clues.summary: Snow-covered coverage is found in the southeast, especially east of Almaty.

clues.title: Landscape: dry shrubby hills, orange grass
text: The landscape in southern Kazakhstan near Uzbekistan is hilly and quite **dry and shrubby**, with a lot of [orange looking grass](https://goo.gl/maps/NMh2NNtw2fLihzkD6). The landscape consists of [dry but grassy rolling hills](https://goo.gl/maps/HVEEsWWCgeKeFyMv7) or [dead flat agricultural land](https://goo.gl/maps/rYuF4Q74ka7y5KXz5) near Zhetisay.
NOTE: These [red and white KM markers](https://goo.gl/maps/55J3nhF75bSt4K7G6) that look like Kyrgyz ones, are only found near Zhetisay.
clues.summary: In the south near Uzbekistan: hilly, dry and shrubby with orange-looking grass, or dead flat farmland near Zhetisay. Red-and-white kilometre markers like Kyrgyz ones are only found near Zhetisay.

differs.how: Red-and-white KM markers here only appear near Zhetisay

clues.title: Landscape: grassy green rolling hills
text: **Grassy** **green rolling hills** can be found in southern Kazakhstan. They are especially common just north of Bishkek.
clues.summary: Grassy green rolling hills in the south, especially just north of the Kyrgyz capital.

clues.title: Vegetation: pine forests with autumn colours
text: Around Semey, you can find small clusters or entire forests** **consisting mostly of **pine trees** and some deciduous trees, which will have **fall colours**.
clues.summary: Small groups or whole forests of mostly pine with some leafy trees showing autumn colours, around the city of Semey.

clues.title: Road: divided asphalt, all white lines
text: The divided section of the **E38** goes **southeast to northwest** from Shymkent to Kyzylorda. The road is made of **asphalt**, and it has **all white road lines**. The landscape varies quite a lot; in the south, it is very [green](https://goo.gl/maps/71g8LgQkJqC4mYJF6) and in the north, it gets [dry, sandy, and shrubby](https://goo.gl/maps/StZ6q6CejmVpK7yg8).
Driving direction: Both ways
clues.summary: A divided asphalt road running southeast to northwest with all white lines. It is green in the south and gets dry, sandy and shrubby in the north. Seen in both directions.

clues.title: Road: under construction, yellow lines
text: The section of the **M36 **going from Karaganda to Almaty can often be recognised by the road being under construction, with a second lane being built. Yellow lines are common. As for the landscape, it’s a wintery dry [steppe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steppe), which looks noticeably [orange-brown](https://goo.gl/maps/7KVHpuL59rVgZVNt9).
Driving direction: **South **from Karaganda.
clues.summary: A road being widened, with yellow lines and a winter-dry, orange-brown steppe. The car drives south from Karaganda.

clues.title: Road: divided highway, yellow edge lines
text: Between Karaganda and Astana, the **M36 **is now a divided highway, with **yellow outer lines**. The landscape consists of a grassy, sometimes hilly, steppe with an occasional row of trees along the road. Note that the general **southeast to northwest** road angle is important.
Driving direction: Both ways
clues.summary: A divided highway with yellow outer lines, running southeast to northwest through grassy, sometimes hilly steppe with occasional tree rows. Seen both ways.

clues.title: Road: divided east-west, hilly steppe
text: The** P4/A17** from Astana to Pavlodar is a divided road, generally going **east to west**, through a **hilly steppe landscape** similar to the M36, but is generally less vegetated**. **Most of the road has **outer yellow lines**.
Driving direction: Both ways
clues.summary: A divided road running east to west through hilly, less green steppe, mostly with yellow outer lines. Seen both ways.

clues.title: Landscape: hazy dead hills
text: The roads from Kyzylagash to Druzhba feature a unique hilly landscape, which looks **hazy** and [dead](https://goo.gl/maps/n1VjdBCmbX9VsuD7A). On most sections, you will see small mountains either [south](https://goo.gl/maps/71N7jRTVjSDqnhyf8) or [east](https://maps.app.goo.gl/FqttjKAp8RPKJzJ69) of the road.
Driving direction: **East **from Kyzylagash.
clues.summary: A hilly landscape that looks hazy and lifeless, with small mountains to the south or east of the road. The car drives east.

clues.title: Road: very bad quality, grey skies
text: The **A26 **goes from Kandyagash to the intersection of M32/E38.

It has very **bad road quality** throughout, ranging from [poor grainy pavement](https://goo.gl/maps/SutyRPAen8GPgGXP7), to [completely unpaved](https://goo.gl/maps/vAPBAKKBSqP1cY4y5). Apart from the northernmost section, the weather is either cloudy or overcast.
The landscape consists mostly of flat, semi-arid grassy plains.
Driving direction: **North **towards Kandyagash. (Mostly)
clues.summary: A road with poor pavement ranging from grainy to completely unpaved, mostly cloudy or overcast, through flat, semi-dry grass plains. Mostly driving north.

clues.title: Road: 6-lane divided highway, quite green
text: The section of the **A1 **going from Astana to Shchuchinsk is a **6-lane divided highway**. The landscape around is generally **quite green**, with trees and grassy plains or hills.
Driving direction: Both ways
clues.summary: A 6-lane divided highway through quite green land with trees, grass plains or hills. Seen in both directions.

clues.title: Road: crumbling edges, single white middle line
text: The **A17 **going to Ulytau Region can be recognised by the **bad pavement quality**, where the edges of the road are almost crumbling away, along with the **single white middle road line**, which can be dashed or solid. The landscape itself is a grassy steppe, with some fall coloured trees occasionally lining the roads.
[West of Atasu](https://goo.gl/maps/TdENdhe3WB985Lhi8), the sun is distinctly low on the horizon.
NOTE: A small section east of Atasu has [pristine new pavement](https://goo.gl/maps/XeJe82NWDfF4gH1K9), which has a slight red tint to it.
Driving direction: **Towards **[**Atasu**](https://www.google.com/maps/@48.6874387,71.6576538,13.19z?entry=ttu) from both directions
clues.summary: Bad pavement with edges almost crumbling, and one white middle line, solid or dashed. Grassy steppe, some autumn trees, a low sun in the west. A short stretch east of the town has new pavement with a red tint.

clues.title: Road: no lines, very dry red-orange land
text: The road north of Zhezqazghan has no road lines. The landscape is **very dry, desolate**, with very limited vegetation** **and slightly hilly. The soil can look very red or orange at times.
The weather is sunny, with a lot of [cumulus clouds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cumulus_cloud).
Driving directions: **North **from Nikolskiy
clues.summary: A road with no road lines through very dry, empty, slightly hilly land with red or orange soil, sunny with cumulus clouds. The car drives north.

clues.title: Road: cracked paving, no lines, overcast steppe
text: The **R260 **road is mostly paved, but not in the best condition; many cracks can be seen, and it** **mostly lacks road lines. The weather is **overcast** and the landscape is a **slightly hilly steppe**, consisting of somewhat yellow grass and reddish soil, which is very evident when the road is [unpaved](https://goo.gl/maps/TdSkNVCsQwfzuWvQ7).

The **R217 **is very similar, but the road is in [better condition](https://goo.gl/maps/gkFt8pTBsvfWYnuq5) and mostly has very [faded dashed white middle road lines](https://goo.gl/maps/sYN29uJEyzQKdJjt7), which are often quite difficult to see. The further east you go, the more [sparse](https://goo.gl/maps/J4zjwGopGaSfr1N3A) the cloud cover gets.
Driving directions: **South **from Atbasar
clues.summary: Mostly paved but cracked road, almost without lines, under overcast skies, in slightly hilly steppe with yellow grass and red soil. A similar road is in better shape with faded dashed white middle lines.

clues.title: Poles: painted bands differ by region
text: These regions/cities have the most useful pole paints you can learn.
The descriptions will be written from top to bottom:
- West Kazakhstan Region uses red, white, and black paint.
- Atyrau Region uses blue, white, and black paint.
- Akmola region has a very thin layer of red, then white, and a thin layer of black on the bottom.
- Kostanay uses a thin layer of turqoise, and yellow.
- Petropavl has a thin layer of white, and light grey.
- Taraz has red, yellow, and black.
- Kyzylorda poles have a thin layer of yellow and red, then white.
- Kyzylorda lamp posts are white, and have turquoise on the bottom.
clues.summary: Pole paint colours (top to bottom) identify regions: west red-white-black, Atyrau blue-white-black, Akmola thin red then white then thin black, Kostanay thin turquoise and yellow, Petropavl white and grey, Taraz red-yellow-black, Kyzylorda thin yellow-red then white.

clues.title: Poles: more painted bands by city
text: These pole paints are less useful than the above hint, but still worth learning if you want to master Kazakhstan.
The descriptions will be written from top to bottom:
- Rudny has red, yellow, red on the top, with white below it.
- Kokshetau uses a few designs, but they all have light blue on the bottom, and sometimes, a thin strip, or two, of yellow on top.
- Shchuchinsk has a thin layer of red, and yellow.
- Ekibastuz has a thin layer of blue, and white
- Shymkent poles have a thin layer of yellow and red, then green.
- Kentau poles have thin layers of blue, yellow, and red, then blue and black below them.
clues.summary: Less useful pole paints: Rudny red-yellow-red over white, Kokshetau light blue bottom, Shchuchinsk thin red and yellow, Ekibastuz blue and white, Shymkent thin yellow-red then green, Kentau blue-yellow-red then blue and black.

clues.title: Bus stops: city-specific designs
text: These are the most useful to learn bus stops.
- Atyrau has a **modern design**, with white and** lime/neon green** walls. The bus stop name is prominently written on top.
- Kostanay uses **simple brown bus stops**, that have a **blue and yellow crest** on one of the glass panes.
- Petropavl also has brown bus stops, with glass panes on all 3 sides not facing the road. The **roof is angled slightly upwards**.
- Karaganda uses old looking **turquoise** bus stops, which have a **curved roof**.
Zhezqazghan has **very wide blue bus stops**, which have **2 sections**; 1 indoors, and one outside. These sections are separated by a door.

images.caption: Map of bus stop designs by city: Kostanay, Petropavl, Atyrau, Karaganda and Zhezqazghan

clues.summary: Useful stops: Atyrau modern white and neon green, Kostanay simple brown with a blue-yellow crest, Petropavl brown with an upward-angled roof, Karaganda old turquoise with a curved roof, Zhezqazghan very wide blue with two sections.

clues.title: Buses: city-specific colours
text: These cities have buses worth learning.
- Aktobe uses **orange and black** buses.
- Zhezqazghan has **orange and white **buses, with “Men ♥ Jezz/Zhez” written on the sides.
- Astana commonly uses these **white**, **black**, and **green **electric buses.
- Karaganda uses** turquoise** buses, just like their bus stops.
- Semey has these **light green** and **white **buses.
- Almaty uses fully green buses, with white patterns and the city name on the sides. Taraz can use similar buses, but they will have “Taraz” written on the sides instead.
clues.summary: Aktobe orange and black, Zhezqazghan orange and white, Astana white-black-green electric, Karaganda turquoise, Semey light green and white, Almaty fully green with white patterns. Taraz buses look similar but say Taraz.

clues.title: Street signs on buildings: city styles
text: These street signs attached to buildings are generally quite inconsistent, but there are some worth knowing.
- Aktobe has compact signs where half of the space is taken by the QR code.
- Petropavl uses white signs, with a blue semicircle below the street names.
- Astana consistently uses this fairly generic design.
- Zhetisay also uses a fairly generic design, but it is not found in Turkistan or Shymkent.
clues.summary: Designs vary, but a few are worth knowing: Aktobe's has half the sign taken by a QR code, Petropavl's is white with a blue semicircle, Astana's is a generic design, and Zhetisay's looks generic but is not found in two other southern cities.

clues.title: Houses: yellow boxes on gas pipes
text: **Yellow boxes **connected to the gas pipes are common outside houses in Shymkent, Turkistan, and Taldykorgan.

images.caption: A yellow box on a gas pipe against a cinder block wall

clues.summary: Yellow boxes on the gas pipes outside houses are common in three southern towns.

clues.title: Lamps: thin grey with two small lights
text: Turkistan consistently uses these **thin grey lamps** with** two small light sources** near the end.
clues.summary: Thin grey lamps with two small light sources near the end are used throughout one southern city.

clues.title: Lamps: sizable blue sensor on top
text: Lamps in Kulsary have a sizable **blue photocell** on the top.
clues.summary: Lamps with a big blue light sensor on top are found in the western town of Kulsary.

clues.title: Lamps: three lamps in a rising row
text: Some lamps in Uralsk have this very unique design, with **3 separate lamps** in an **ascending pattern**.
clues.summary: Some lamps have three separate lights in an ascending pattern, in the western city of Uralsk.

clues.title: Houses: dirt line on the right of the roof
text: East of Aktobe, there is a **vertical line of dirt** on the right side of the roof.

images.caption: Red oval marks a dirt line on the right of the Google car roof

clues.summary: A vertical line of dirt on the right side of a roof, east of Aktobe.

clues.title: Coverage: dense pine forests
text: Coverage in dense **baltic pine forests** can be found north of Shchuchinsk, which is north of Astana.
NOTE: Baltic pines can be found in other parts of the country.
clues.summary: Coverage in dense pine forests is found north of the town Shchuchinsk, north of Astana. Pines also grow in other parts of the country.

clues.title: Coverage: hazy forest-fire smoke
text: Parts of Oskemen have **hazy forest fire coverage**.
clues.summary: Parts of the eastern city Oskemen have coverage with hazy forest-fire smoke.

clues.title: Coverage: snowy mountains in a southern city
text: In southern Almaty City, there is **snow** coverage **in the mountains**.
clues.summary: In the south of the biggest city there is snow-covered mountain coverage.

clues.title: Landscape: barren grass
text: The Altyn Emel National Park is a barren grassland with snowy mountains in all directions. Some parts are [very snowy](https://goo.gl/maps/7K5s7XqLSKzpMLvEA). And in the eastern section, there is a small [curvy mountain pass](https://goo.gl/maps/8rJPLHV5Zs7DxQC87).
clues.summary: A barren grassland with snowy mountains in every direction, some parts very snowy. In the east there is a small curvy mountain pass. This is a national park in the southeast.

clues.title: Coverage: only May coverage, sunny
text: The only **May coverage** in Kazakhstan is found in the Almaty exclave of Alataou, which is east of Almaty proper. All of the coverage is sunny and the mountains are visible to the south.
clues.summary: The only coverage shot in May is in a small area east of the biggest city. It is all sunny, with mountains visible to the south.

clues.title: Landscape: ridge of hills to the north
text: A small ridge of **hills **is visible to the **north **in a lot of Taldykorgan coverage.
clues.summary: A low ridge of hills is visible to the north in much of the coverage of the southeastern town Taldykorgan.

clues.title: Road: unpaved sandy desert road, blinding bright
text: Near the Turkmenistan border in southwest Kazakhstan, you will find this **unpaved sandy desert road. **The landscape is almost blindingly bright from the sand.
clues.summary: An unpaved sandy desert road near the Turkmenistan border in the southwest, with a landscape that is almost blindingly bright from the sand.
